title: The aesthetics of comparativeness in Islam Observed
core_idea: The article investigates how an interdisciplinary comparative methodology—drawing on anthropology, ethnography, sociology, and literature—is used in Islam Observed to trace the foundational formation and diverse practices of Islam in Morocco and Indonesia, with particular focus on aesthetic codes and the role of cultural poetics, and it critically examines the literary aura of this comparative approach in light of recent theories in comparative and world literature.
tldr: Examines the use of interdisciplinary comparative methods in Islam Observed to illuminate regional variations in Islamic practice via aesthetic codes and cultural poetics, and critically engages the literary dimensions of that comparative approach.
